# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for answering detailed questions)

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE PRINCESS OF THE ATOM — Ray Cummings (Gutenberg 75690; Avon reprint 1950; orig. 1929 Munsey)

**Dedication:** to Hal (son) and Russ (son-in-law), both chemists.
**Blurb:** "Her Love Destroyed One World and Threatened Another!" Giants off New England; Dianne; Dr. Ferrule; Frank & Drake Ferrule; Togaro "the man who would rule the universe."

**Prologue (narrator Frank Ferrule, 17):** Family: father Dr. Ferrule (consulting chemist, ~50, iron-gray hair, horn-rimmed spectacles, slender, studious); mother (died when Frank a child, the year after the island incident); brother Drake (6 yrs older, 6'2", stalwart blond, "huge dog" good nature; age 23 at the event, 28 later); sister Dianne (blue-eyed flaxen-haired child; at 16 exquisite, "cameo"/"pastel" beauty). Frank: small, slender, dark hair, excitable, "terrier."
- August 14 (fateful morning), summer home on Maine coast, King's Cove. Father doing chemical experiment. Kids rowed dory to **Bird's Nest Island** (~2 miles offshore; few hundred acres; 50-ft central rock peak; gulls; spring of fresh water; childhood signal flag and signal fire on peak).
- Swim: Frank ducked Dianne; she cried "Frank, stop that! Let me go!" when he clung to her hair at forehead. Her hair grows in a queer peak at forehead; she wears it parted far to side.
- Dianne vanished from beach; clothes left in pile. No boat seen. Never found.
- Father's revelation: Dianne was a foundling found ~15 years earlier (when Frank ~2, Drake ~8, the year before mother died) on Bird's Nest Island in a thicket by father & mother; ~1-year-old infant; no one claimed. Infant robe: long-sleeved, tiny hood, gossamer golden fabric "like spun gold," kept in father's desk drawer. Crescent-moon silver-sheen scar on forehead under hair peak. Named Dianne by mother. Father trained her to hide it. Father: "wondered if she were just exactly human."
- The vanishing was **five years before** the giants.

**Ch I – Coming of the Giants:** First giant reported March 20 by small steamship out of Halifax (bound Portland), near Cape Sable, Nova Scotia; full moon; giant waist-deep, bullet-headed, pale close-cut hair, naked chest; followed ship. Later giants late March off Maine (near Penobscot), up to Bay of Fundy. Frank is pilot for International Mail Service (Boston–St. John). Chief sends him, senior pilot, with relief pilot **Bob (Jones)** and radio operator **Green**, to patrol at 1000 ft. Frank sees giant at cove near Bird's Nest Island/ their summer cove; giant kills people on cliff with arm sweep; two dead. Giant shrinks, swims toward Bird's Nest Island, dives, disappears. Green receives message: father has heard from Dianne; come to Bennett Field, NY.

**Ch II – Mysterious Visitor:** Westchester home (small village). Before midnight a man thumps on door; tall bulky, long dark overcoat, black felt hat, hairless heavy jaw, ~35, foreign soft voice. Asks for Dr. Ferrule; "You had a daughter—" re Dianne. Sits awkwardly like never seen a chair. Says "I came to warn you"; "stay away from your house in Maine"; giants "dangerous"; "You will never see Dianne again. Forget her." Leaves; wears hat backward; stoops at doorways. Drake wanted to pursue; father calls him back.

**Ch III – Signal Fire:** Frank arrives early morning. Father deduces visitor was a giant. Frank, father, Drake, return to Maine by official plane; permit; town of **Elton** (2 miles from home) under military rule; officer knows father. Father has automatic. Night watch. Next morning at dawn: smoke signal from Bird's Nest Island — the childhood signal: **two large puffs, then three smaller, then two large** (blanket over fire).

**Ch IV – Strange Island:** Drake & Frank row over (dory from boathouse; oilskins; rifle; automatics). Father stays. On island: embers, wet sticks; fern moves; tiny figures; a woman an inch-ish tall, golden robe, face "size of finger nail"; Frank: "Dianne, it's you!"

**Ch V – Princess of the Atom:** Dianne grows (drinks drug pellet). With companion **Ahlma** (silver-white robe, paler crescent, golden hair; Dianne's servant and friend). Dianne: "Ahlma—enough!" Togaro: leader of giants, "Togaro"; he's the midnight visitor (accent matches Ahlma's). Dianne explains: she was born in an atom-world; parents' throne threatened by a conqueror (Togaro); scientists spirited her away with drug and flying vehicle; left her on Earth. Togaro took her back into smallness 5 years ago; she was rescued; now ruler. Togaro wants Earth to conquer, wants Dianne. Father wants atom-fragment brought to King's Cove; they must guard it. In the house (curtain/rug at door): Togaro, tiny, in corner; flees; Dianne, Drake, Frank take pellets to chase him into smallness.

**Ch VI – Chase into Smallness:** Dianne gives pellets ("sweetish" taste). Frank & Drake shrink with Dianne in bedroom; cellular caverns, rock plain, tumbled terrain; the knothole is a "caldron." Dianne: trip to her world "three or four days." Drake took too big a dose? (Ch VII.) Togaro (~a man; white shirt, massive hairy chest) lures them into a cavern; grows.

**Ch VII – Flight in Cellular Caverns:** Drake gulps full pellet, fights Togaro, both grow giant; through roof opening; Drake nearly crushed; Ahlma and father see Togaro/Drake; Drake faints; Togaro attacks father and Ahlma; Ahlma flings lamp (extinguished); Togaro flees house.

**Ch VIII – Death of the Giants:** Return to normal size; afternoon; Frank talks with Dianne. Night: back to island with father's automatic. Embers; meteorite buried (copper-colored, scarred, ~ton); Dianne shows tiny crater "pin-point" for descent. Storm; six giants on island; battle with planes and battleship; bombs; giants die (one falls off, others killed); one giant escapes to mainland and dies 10 miles down coast. Dianne says goodbye; Drake shrinks away ("Togaro may have gone into the atom... stupid brutes he sacrificed"). Frank chips off fragment with claspknife (chunk few inches across). Men capture Frank: "Ferrule. ... King's Cove."

**Ch IX – Tiny Fragment of Rock:** A year later; Frank & father live at King's Cove; fragment in special barred room, slab, microscope, guards. May: a tiny man waves white flag.

**Ch X – White Flag:** Room sealed; granite slab 6-ft square; dome light; microscope; atomizers/poisons. Guard **Foley** (armed; 3 guards rotate; Ransome later). Figure: **Alt**, bloody, bound feet, says "Friend—friend—from Drake." Says Drake sent him; wants weapons (steel knife, automatics); princess and Lady Ahlma waiting in flying car. Alt's accent like Ahlma/Togaro. Frank agrees to go in with Alt.

**Ch XI – Giant in Ambush:** Frank: bathing suit, drug belt (8 compartments each side, two drugs of opposite action, 8 intensities). Carries four automatics and knives; holsters. Father lifts them on slab; Frank feels a tug at shoelace and something crawling on shoulder (later significant — Togaro rode on Frank's belt/shoe). Crescent pit; giant in ambush climbs from pit.

**Ch XII – The Meeting:** Frank shoots giant (automatic) twice; hides in cleft; giant withdraws. Frank realizes small man (thumbnail-sized) clinging to his belt — Togaro; escapes. Journey: metallic plain, rain, tiny forest. Red signal light; **Drake** found; kisses from Dianne ("Frank, dear"). Frank: she's "just a girl" now.

**Ch XIII – The Stowaway:** Flying car (40 ft long, elliptical windows, woven wire hull, ductile metal; contracts with current). Frank sits in small room with Dianne. Drake explains: Togaro's group of renegade leaders ("half a million followers" to conquer Earth; plan transport via a larger ship). Ahlma's cry warns: automatic dragged by tiny Togaro (8–10 inches tall) toward door; he escapes into smallness. Togaro is a stowaway.

**Ch XIV – The Locked Door:** Voyage ~15–20 hours; molecules; spectrometer guidance (Drake); bow attractive/stern repulsive for gravity. Sees stars; a "round" molecule-sun; Drake: "we dare not disturb orbit." Guard in passage murdered with tiny bodkin-sword in heart (Togaro). Girls' stateroom door locked.

**Ch XV – Togaro at Bay:** Ahlma unconscious; Dianne gone (Togaro forced drug on her, both dwindling). Shout from opposite cabin; Dianne's voice "Frank!"; Togaro's sardonic laugh behind locked door.

**Ch XVI – Frank's Plan:** Door broken; Togaro sitting wedged, holding Dianne; threatens to take enlarging pellet; Drake and Frank stand down; Frank's plan: Frank shrinks, goes in under Togaro's room and distracts; Drake shoots Togaro. Frank takes diminishing drug.

**Ch XVII – Tiny Prowler:** Drake signals; Frank ~1 inch; climbs Togaro's trousers rope-like; fails; grows to strike; Togaro lurches; Drake shouts; Frank clings to Togaro's belt.

**Ch XVIII – Escape of Togaro:** Togaro takes enlarging drug, breaks ceiling, leaps from ship to ground with Dianne in arm; Frank rides on his belt. Ship landed near **Mita**'s largest city (Shore City).

Planet data: "Mita," globe ~300 miles diameter, sun ~20 million miles, rotation ~6h40m, one moon. Heavy metallic rock.

**Ch XIX – Night of Turmoil:** Crowd demands drugs; Jain (huge black-coated official); Drake and Ahlma and Alt; palace (two stories, dome, spire, lakeside cliff). Togaro's headquarters on a park island (3 miles across lake). Drake organizes expedition of young men.

**Ch XX – Blood Light of Dawn:** Mob chanting "The world ends tonight! Give us the drugs!" Drake, Ahlma, Alt grow atop palace spire. At dawn, giants rise from city and island; Togaro's monstrous ship expands, flies off. Togaro's giants carry tens of thousands of people (small) into ship; city wrecked.

**Ch XXI – Riding the Giant:** Frank rode Togaro, climbed rope to Dianne's cabin; hid on cushion; Dianne passes him; Togaro's threat: "Vengeance of Togaro!"

**Ch XXII – "Vengeance of Togaro!":** Dianne hides Frank in her robe; Togaro plans to kill Mitans; ship grounds on shallows near island; Togaro says they'll stay and "grow a little larger" on Mita. Dianne wants to get Frank out.

**Ch XXIII – Doomed Little Planet!:** Togaro's ship lifts from Mita; tosses Mita into the sun's path; planet falls toward sun.

**Ch XXIV – End of a World:** Drake takes charge of rescue; Ahlma goes to bring refugees; ~110,000 Mitans rescued; Mita destroyed by falling into sun (Drake's ship escapes).

**Ch XXV – In the Campfire Light:** Togaro's ship lands in a forest encampment (~40,000 people; 600–800 Togarite leaders). Frank disguised in a jacket and cone hat; sneaks to Dianne's tent. Togaro (sash, tasseled leggings, discards drug belt) at supper with Dianne. Frank strikes Togaro with rock; Dianne fights; escape with drugs.

**Ch XXVI – Black and White Flags:** Frank & Dianne in the abyss; black-and-white striped flag (Dianne made it on ship). Drake, Ahlma, Alt reunite with them. They climb out to rock summit. They find rock stolen; room is different; Togaro's men guard it.

**Ch XXVII – Fight on the Rock Summit:** Four Togarites; Alt waves flag, then fight; Alt stabbed (bar in side) — unconscious; Drake's automatic; four enemies killed/stunned; bodies hidden.

**Ch XXVIII – Return to Earth:** Escape through rock room door; Togaro comes out with Togarite hordes; they escape to **King's Cove boathouse** at night under moon.

**Ch XXIX – Theft of the Rock:** Backstory: Foley killed; father knocked unconscious; rock stolen; night of May 14 (Alt & Frank left), ~May 20 Togarites emerge. Father taken to Portland and Washington.

**Ch XXX – World at Bay:** May 21 giants (~200 ft) rise at King's Cove; spread through Elton; Lynn destroyed; battleship sunk by Togaro; Canadian planes shot down by sling rocks; Portland occupied May 23; advance south.

**Ch XXXI – Togaro Strikes:** June 1–2: New Haven trampled; Bear Mountain Bridge torn; Togaro (~titanic) at Sandy Hook demands surrender; wrecks Lower Manhattan; orders fleets to Maine; message from Drake: "Don't yield! We're coming with the drugs." Attack on Togarite lines at New Jersey; Dianne visible rising from the sea.

**Ch XXXII – The Fugitives:** Frank, Drake, Ahlma, Dianne escape across Maine and Connecticut; Dianne runs at night toward coast; Frank follows.

**Ch XXXIII – Combat of Titans:** Drake & Ahlma reach Mount Vernon by plane; Drake phones "Don't yield—I have the drugs." Frank & Dianne grow large, wade the Sound, face Togaro at Sandy Hook; Frank fights Togaro; Dianne helps; Togaro swallows poison; drops fragment-globe into the sea ("your damned Mitans lose"); Togaro dies, falls across Highlands and Lower Bay.

**Ch XXXIV – Princess of the Cottage:** A year later; Dianne & Frank at cottage by sea; Drake & Ahlma nearby; father in NYC. Togaro's body sunk; Togarites (40,000) isolated on an island; drugs destroyed. Frank & Dianne: "Frank Ferrule, you can make your own smoke signals for Drake and Ahlma. I'm going to bed."

**Ad:** "A SCIENCE-FICTION MASTERPIECE"; Avon Fantasy Novels series; Donald A. Wollheim.

## BOOK 2 of 2: POPPY OTT'S PEDIGREED PICKLES — Leo Edwards (Gutenberg 71240; Grosset & Dunlap 1927; illus. Bert Salg)

**Characters:** Narrator **Jerry Todd** (vice-president; Mother, Dad; Dad's brickyard). **Poppy Ott** (president; tall long-legged; ideas; father **Mr. Ott** (shiftless tramp reformed, now runs stilt factory)). **Forrest Pennykorn** (rich snob, sporty roadster, "smarty"; grandson). **Mr. Foreman Pennykorn** (banker/canning factory president; Canners Exchange Bank); son **Norman Pennykorn** (runs canning factory). **Mr. Simon Weckler** (old widower, cistern cat **Peter**, yellow cat; housekeeper **Mrs. Clayton**; daughter **Clara** eloped with Nathan Weir). **Butch McGinty** (towing/house-moving mule driver "Jerusalem"; pickle genius; Zulutown; "I swan!"). **Widow Cora O'Mally** (cucumber patch; old Weir house in river bottoms; Irish dialect "ye", "'tis"). **Bill Hadley** (town marshal). **Mr. Thomas Lorring** (banker, Commercial Bank; stilt partner). **Doc Leland** (pill case; old Lizzie). **Mr. Stair** (newspaper editor, Tutter Daily Globe). **Peoria chief of police** telegram. **Mr. Wiggins** (Rockford wholesale, Wiggins & Wakefield). **Mr. Silas Hartenbower** (102-year-old centenarian; told of iron mold/lead cucumber). **Uncle Abner Weir** (cane, fringe whiskers, nightgown; Rimtown, Ohio; scold). **Tommy (Tom) Weir** (grandson, big black eyes, hot-tempered). **Nathan Weir** (Tom's father; one-armed; cat killer; jewel robbery Peoria; died in hospital). **Old Peg-leg Weir** (river pirate; built stone house; cucumber hobby; iron mold). **Spider Whickleberry** (rigged the strangling-machine contraption). **Mrs. Bagley, Mrs. Brown, Mrs. Morgan, Mrs. Hempline, Mrs. Cook, Mrs. Hiram Springer, Mrs. Bowman, Mrs. Clayton (Mrs. Clayton bought pickles)**. **Mr. Samson** (railroad food buyer), **Mr. Lorrimer** (railroad president).

**Setup:** Poppy's "Pickle Parlor" idea; Frank/Jerry argues "Pickles is pickles." Stilt factory history (Seven-League Stilts). Store: empty building near Lattimer meat market, rent $125/month (Pennykorn's). Overheard at bank: Pennykorns plan to buy Ashton plant; Dandy Dills; Mrs. O'Mally corn/cucumbers; Pennykorns' 50,000 dollars goal; sweet corn $9/ton vs Ashton $10.50.

**Events in order:**
1. Poppy's pickle parlor scheme; bank; ad mis-printed "Seven diamonds worth ten thousand dollars" (proofreader slug error); ad "WHOSE PICKLES," Box 9, Tutter Daily Globe.
2. Poppy's "Silent" partner: Mr. Weckler (cistern cat rescue); offers old playhouse; $5/month rent; "pay in pickles."
3. Poppy's pickle jar (bought at Presbyterian missionary food sale at Drake's store); 63 letters; 54 letters; women; broom attack by a woman on Jerry; Dr. Jekyl/Hyde talk.
4. Jerry poisoned (Dad's pickles); Doc Leland.
5. Burglar strews pickles in Dorm cellar; one-armed burglar.
6. Butch McGinty (pickle genius; hired $3.50/day; cash; recipe secret; Aunt Jemima scheme; handbill "AUNT JEMIMA'S PICKLES").
7. Mrs. O'Mally cucumbers ($2/bushel; 4 bushels first purchase); Mrs. O'Mally's fright (sounds in cellar).
8. Store moved to Mr. Weckler's lot (across from canning factory, 224 South Main Street); Norman Pennykorn complains; "Poppy's Pickle Parlor, The Green and Yellow Store."
9. Ptomaine poisoning epidemic (Methodist church supper; stuffed olives; Mrs. Higgins); Jerry & Poppy's sample pickles blamed.
10. Weckler attacked in library (cat strangled; Peter killed; cat tail); gold cucumber found in flower bed; one-armed robber.
11. Cat killer Tommy; secret chimney door; tunnel; Uncle Abner's cave; Tom's bargain.
12. Pennykorn threatens; Poppy's "pedigreed pickles" name.
13. Lorring's $500 loan; ladies' aid; Pennykorn's crooked letter; contract attempt in bank; Poppy's sales trip; Chicago orders ($6000+); treasure found in Mr. Weckler's? (iron chest under shadow of chimney; $35,000 total; $7,000 each to four).
14. Pennykorn gives stock in new pickle company (50 shares each). Banquet; Poppy never said a word. Tom reunited with grandpa Mr. Weckler; Uncle Abner marries Mrs. O'Mally; Butch got steady job up canal.
15. Next book: POPPY OTT AND THE FRECKLED GOLDFISH.

Notes on Jerry Todd's narration: uses "Dad's saying: Every day a little fun and a little business." Recognized Mr. Weckler at bank.
